samples.summary: New MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH duplicates the existing MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH cap in the same package
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111` already exports `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` — documented as "Nesting cap for bandBlockNumerics' own walk… A table cell's `blocks` can hold another table, whose cells hold another — a chain a peer can write to any depth" — i.e. exactly the same question (how deep may nested tables be read) with the same value, in the same model directory, and already written up in the canonical subsystem doc (`docs/design/docs/docs.md:290-298`). The diff adds a second, differently-named constant in a brand-new module rather than reusing or extending it, and the two already give different answers at the cap: `bandBlockNumerics` "stops descending and leaves what is below as stored", while `treeNodeToBlock` drops the rows entirely. `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:40` carries a third copy (`MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 32`) whose stated justification for being a copy (dependency direction slides → docs) does not apply to this new docs-side constant. Two/three caps for one invariant will drift.

samples.summary: Hard nesting cap contradicts a stated Goal of docs-nested-tables.md, and no design doc is updated
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:19-20` lists under Goals: "Recursive nesting with no hard depth limit (UI naturally limits via minimum cell width of 30 px)". This change introduces exactly such a hard limit (32) in the CRDT reader, the frontend reader and the layout, and truncates rows beyond it. Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline this data-model constraint should be folded into the canonical docs (`docs-nested-tables.md` Goals/Risks, and the band section of `docs/design/docs/docs.md` which already enumerates MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH and the peer-attribute banding rules). The diff updates no design doc at all — the new cap, the cell-range clamp and the blockParentMap cycle guards are recorded only in source comments.

samples.summary: Sixth hand-rolled blockParentMap parent-chain walk; no shared helper despite the diff's own rationale against duplicating resolution
samples.evidence: The change adds `walkToTopLevelBlockId` (selection.ts:161) and `findOutermostTableId` (text-editor.ts:3914) while leaving inline copies of the same loop in `table-layout.ts:510` (resolveNestedTableLayout), `peer-cursor.ts:129`, `text-editor.ts:3891` (findOuterCellAddress) and `model/range-slices.ts:80` (`topLevelBlockId`, which already carried the same `seen` guard), plus the recursive variant `Doc.findBlockInCells`. Each now carries its own copy of the cycle guard, with divergent cycle semantics (resolveNestedTableLayout returns `undefined`; walkToTopLevelBlockId returns the id it stopped on). The diff's own comment (`text-editor.ts:129-131`) says resolving a gesture two ways is what produced #1049, yet the walk itself stays duplicated across six sites — the new `model/table-nesting.ts` would have been a natural home.

samples.summary: Nested-table lookup idiom copied at four call sites instead of one helper
samples.evidence: `layout.blocks.find(...)?.block.tableData ?? resolveNestedTableLayout(id, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` is written out verbatim in `selection.ts:189-191`, `selection.ts:833-835`, `selection.ts:861-866` and `text-editor.ts:4331-4333`. This is the actual fix for #1049 — the bug was precisely one site knowing about nested tables and another not — so the fix reproduces the failure mode's shape: a fifth consumer (e.g. `editor.ts:1783`, `text-editor.ts:2859`, `table-merge-context.ts:47`) is one flat lookup away from regressing. A single `findTableDataForLayout(blockId, layout)` exported alongside `resolveNestedTableLayout` would make the rule mechanical.

samples.summary: Peer-written cell rectangle is clamped in the view normalizer only, not at the model read boundary the band discipline prescribes
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs.md:212-260` states the rule for peer-writable numbers: band them where they enter the model ("applied at both read boundaries") and bound the loop that consumes them. `normalizeCellRange` clamps in `view/selection.ts`, but the model-side consumers of a `tableCellRange` still loop over the raw indices — `range-runs.ts:80-82` (`visitCellRectangleSlices`), `editor.ts:1787-1799` and `text-editor.ts:2863-2875` all take `Math.min/max(cr.start…, cr.end…)` of unclamped values. Only `buildCellRangeRects` got the second-half loop bound. If a rectangle can reach those paths (restored/persisted selection is copied verbatim at `editor.ts:2487-2492`), the invariant holds in one layer and not the other.

samples.summary: Substantial hardening program bundled into a #1049 selection bug fix
samples.evidence: The stated issue (#1049) is about cell-rectangle selection/copy inside nested tables and across merges. Alongside that fix the change ships an unrelated denial-of-service program: a new nesting-cap module and its export, caps in two CRDT readers and the layout recursion, cycle guards in five parent-chain walks (`table-layout.ts`, `peer-cursor.ts`, `selection.ts`, `text-editor.ts` x2, `document.ts`), and peer cell-range clamping — plus a dedicated test file for the cap. None of that is needed for the reported outcome, it touches a different subsystem concern (peer-attribute banding, documented separately in `docs/design/docs/docs.md`), and it makes the selection fix harder to review and to revert independently.

samples.summary: Read-time truncation of over-deep nesting can be written back, destroying rows
samples.evidence: Both readers drop all rows of a table at the cap, and the frontend store's model is what subsequent edits are serialized from (`docs-tables.md` notes `updateTableAttrs` is "Whole-block replacement"). A document whose nesting exceeds the cap (only reachable from a hostile peer or an exotic import, so user impact is small) therefore reads as truncated and can be persisted truncated, which is data loss rather than the "degrade, do not vanish" behaviour the module header claims and the opposite of the sibling cap's rule (`MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` explicitly "leaves what is below as stored").

finding.summary: New MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH duplicates the existing MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH cap in the same package
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111` already exports `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` — documented as "Nesting cap for bandBlockNumerics' own walk… A table cell's `blocks` can hold another table, whose cells hold another — a chain a peer can write to any depth" — i.e. exactly the same question (how deep may nested tables be read) with the same value, in the same model directory, and already written up in the canonical subsystem doc (`docs/design/docs/docs.md:290-298`). The diff adds a second, differently-named constant in a brand-new module rather than reusing or extending it, and the two already give different answers at the cap: `bandBlockNumerics` "stops descending and leaves what is below as stored", while `treeNodeToBlock` drops the rows entirely. `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:40` carries a third copy (`MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 32`) whose stated justification for being a copy (dependency direction slides → docs) does not apply to this new docs-side constant. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the working tree. `packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26` is a brand-new single-constant module exporting `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32`, while `packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111` already exports `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` in the same package and same `model/` directory, with a doc comment (lines 97-110) describing the same peer-written nested-table chain hazard. The new module's own comment (table-nesting.ts:14-17) names `numeric-attrs.ts` as the analogous guard yet neither imports nor references the existing constant. The two already answer the same question differently at the cap: `numeric-attrs.ts:408` stops descending and leaves deeper content as stored, whereas `crdt-tree.ts:224-229` substitutes `[]` for the rows. `packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:40` is a third copy, and the canonical doc `docs/design/docs/docs.md:292-298` justifies that copy specifically on dependency direction (slides -> docs) — a justification that cannot apply to a new docs-side constant sitting next to `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`. `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` is absent from all of `docs/design/`, so the canonical subsystem doc still describes only two caps. Duplication/reuse is squarely in the design-fit lane; no guard elsewhere reconciles the constants, so no refutation ground applies. Whether the severity is best read as major (caps that drift would leave deep tables materialized but unbanded) or minor is arguable, but that ambiguity is not grounds to drop the finding.
